RESOLVED with live-verified evidence, not just documentation reading. The 'classic' endpoint (/aq/observation/latLong/current/) most training data/tutorials reference is being retired by EPA on 2026-09-30 -- found via a dated, merged pyairnow PR migrating for exactly this reason, confirmed directly against EPA's own official PDF notice (AirNowAPIUpdates2026June.pdf), then confirmed live with an actual test query.

Correct endpoint: GET https://www.airnowapi.org/aq/observation/current/ziplatlong/ (?format=application/json&latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}&API_KEY={key}). Response: JSON array, one object per pollutant: dateObserved, hourObserved (string 'HH:MM'), localTimeZone, reportingAreaName, siteID, siteName, parameterName, nowcastAQI, aqiCategoryName, reportingAgency, lookupBehavior, consideredMonitors, lookupBoundary. Error shape: {"WebServiceError":[{"Message":"..."}]}. Empty array = no data.

Answers all four original questions: (a) NowCast AQI -- yes, nowcastAQI field. (b) full per-pollutant breakdown -- yes, one array entry per pollutant. (c) owning agency name for attribution -- yes, reportingAgency field, confirmed present and populated ('Bay Area Air District') in a live response, directly answering bluegull-aqi-10h.15 with no fallback needed for the common case. (d) category descriptor -- yes, aqiCategoryName (no numeric Category.Number in the raw response, unlike the retiring endpoint -- derive the number from the TAD table if needed, that's classification of a received value, not computing an AQI, per bluegull-aqi-10h.17).

Recorded in doc/DESIGN.md 'Backend service' architecture section since both the backend (bluegull-aqi-q9r.2) and AirNowDirectClient need this same endpoint.

Implemented and verified end-to-end, not just unit tested. aqi_lookup.get_aqi() (core logic, plain function) checks the DynamoDB cache, falls back to airnow_client.fetch_current_observations() against the real (2026-migrated) AirNow endpoint on a miss, caches the result. lambda_handler.py is a thin wrapper: parses queryStringParameters, basic presence/type validation (400 on missing/non-numeric lat/lon -- full coverage-area validation is q9r.30), calls aqi_lookup, returns 200/502 without echoing AirNow's raw error message.

Verified for real: 14 pytest tests pass (AirNow client parsing stubbed, cache tests against real DynamoDB Local not moto, handler tests), pylint 10/10, sam validate and sam build both pass with dependencies actually landing in the build artifact. Then ran bin/run_local.py (the native local runner, q9r.12) against the LIVE AirNow API with Steve's real key: first request was a genuine cache miss returning real San Francisco PM2.5/OZONE readings including reportingAgency='Bay Area Air District', second request was a genuine cache hit (cached:true) with zero additional AirNow calls. Error paths (missing params, non-numeric) verified live too.

AIRNOW_API_KEY resolution: env var first (local dev), else SSM parameter (production) -- fetched once per cold start and memoized, per q9r.18's guidance, not re-fetched per request.

AqiCacheTable added to template.yaml: PAY_PER_REQUEST billing (on-demand, per the Scaling & Performance section), single hash key LocationKey (S), TTL on ExpiresAt. sam validate and sam build both pass with this resource in place. Cache code (bluegull-aqi-q9r.2) reads/writes it via CACHE_TABLE_NAME, populated by the template from !Ref AqiCacheTable rather than hardcoded.

Implemented and verified. Lambda execution role now has a scoped IAM policy (ssm:GetParameter on the exact parameter ARN, kms:Decrypt on alias/aws/ssm) -- least privilege, not a wildcard. aqi_lookup._resolve_airnow_api_key() reads AIRNOW_API_KEY env var first (local dev via .env), falls back to SSM's GetParameter(WithDecryption=True) using AIRNOW_API_KEY_SSM_PARAMETER (template env var holding the parameter NAME, not the secret itself). Resolved key is memoized at module scope so warm invocations don't re-fetch it every request. The parameter itself (/bluegull-aqi/airnow-api-key) was already verified created in AWS during a previous session; this closes the code-side consumption of it.

service/bin/dynamodb_local.py: setup/start/stop for DynamoDB Local, downloaded on demand from AWS's official S3 distribution (never vendored into git -- ~130MB unpacked, nothing else in this repo commits binaries). Simpler than Plant-Tracer's bin/local_services.py by design: that script generically manages three services (DynamoDB Local, MinIO, Mailpit); this project only needs one, so a single-purpose script is clearer than a one-service instance of a multi-service abstraction. Verified: downloaded, extracted, started, and confirmed responding correctly via both a raw curl smoke test and real boto3 calls. tests/conftest.py auto-starts it via a session-scoped fixture, so  needs no manual setup step.

service/bin/run_local.py: serves lambda_handler over plain HTTP (Python's http.server, no Flask dependency needed for something this small), translating each request into the API Gateway HTTP API v2 event shape. Auto-starts DynamoDB Local, creates the local cache table if missing, loads .env itself (minimal parser, no new dependency) with sensible local-dev defaults for CACHE_TABLE_NAME/DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT_URL/AWS_REGION so  needs no manual env setup beyond a real AIRNOW_API_KEY. Verified end-to-end against the live AirNow API: cache miss returning real data, cache hit avoiding a second AirNow call, and both error paths (missing params, non-numeric) -- all confirmed live, not just asserted.
